definition: The term evolvability is a framework of computational learning introduced by Leslie Valiant in his paper of the same name.
details: The aim of this theory is to model biological evolution and categorize which types of mechanisms are evolvable. Evolution is an extension of PAC learning and learning from statistical queries.

explainer.lead: Evolvability is a way to study evolution as a learning process. Introduced by Leslie Valiant, it asks which evolutionary mechanisms can improve through this process, connecting biological evolution with computational learning theory.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making paper airplanes, keeping the designs that fly farther, and then trying small changes to those designs. Evolvability asks when this kind of repeated tinkering can be understood as learning, and which ways of changing can actually lead to improvement. It studies the process rather than building a better airplane itself.
tiers.practitioner: Treat evolvability as a theoretical modeling framework, not an optimization library. To apply it, describe the evolutionary mechanism as a learning problem and analyze it in relation to PAC learning and statistical queries. A simulation that improves over generations does not by itself establish that the mechanism is evolvable in this formal sense.
tiers.paperLevel: Evolvability is a computational learning framework introduced by Leslie Valiant in his paper of the same name. It models biological evolution and categorizes evolvable mechanisms by extending PAC learning and learning from statistical queries; it is a learning model, not a numerical evolvability score.

explainer.example: Consider a population of simple swimmers in which small inherited changes can improve swimming speed. Model the repeated variation and selection as a learning process, then ask whether that mechanism fits the evolvability framework; this separates the formal question from merely observing that some swimmers became faster.

usedIn.name: Computational learning theory
usedIn.detail: Provides a framework for studying biological evolution through learning.

usedIn.name: Models of biological evolution
usedIn.detail: Supports analysis of which evolutionary mechanisms can be classified as evolvable.

explainer.intuition: Evolution can be viewed as a learner that changes through repeated variation and selection. Evolvability asks which mechanisms make that learning process possible.
howItWorks: Start with a biological evolutionary mechanism.
Express its adaptive process as a learning problem.
Relate the model to PAC learning and statistical queries.
Determine whether the mechanism is evolvable within the framework.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives researchers a learning-theoretic language for comparing evolutionary mechanisms rather than treating every adaptive process as equally evolvable. It also places evolution in relation to PAC learning and statistical-query learning.
misconceptions: It is not a software tool or optimization algorithm.
It is not a numerical score for how adaptable a system is.
Observed improvement alone does not establish formal evolvability.
